app/Services/CarrierClient.php:59 connectTimeout equals the full per-attempt timeout (1.4s), so it adds nothing. A shorter connect timeout would let a dead host fail faster

app/Http/Controllers/ShippingQuoteController.php:15-24 maps the domain exceptions in the controller. Fine, but UnknownPostcode could render itself

strengths: Http client used correctly: baseUrl, withToken, acceptJson, a timeout on each attempt, retry(3, 100, when) that retries only ConnectionException and 5xx. 401 and 404 are not retried (probe confirmed: 500 then 401 gives 2 calls and 1 report; 429 gives 1 call and the fallback)
Time budget documented in one tight comment: 3 x 1.4s + 2 x 100ms = 4.4s
401 is reported through report() with the original RequestException, then the fallback is served
A malformed 200 body leads to the fallback
Tests use modern helpers: Http::preventStrayRequests, Sleep::fake (suite runs in about 0.2s), Exceptions::fake with assertReported/assertReportedCount/assertNothingReported, and named datasets
Tests cover leading zeros, array input, no retry on 404, recovery after 5xx and after a connection failure, exhausted retries for both, configured fallback price, and the 401 path

app/Exceptions/CarrierUnavailable.php:8 ShouldntReport on an exception that is always caught inside the app is unnecessary noise

tests/Feature/ShippingQuoteTest.php: no Sleep::fake, so retry tests really sleep (suite takes about 1.4s vs 0.2s). No Http::preventStrayRequests either, and the invalid-postcode test asserts nothing sent without having faked Http
strengths: Compact CarrierClient: one fluent chain with a timeout on each attempt (1.4s), a shorter connect timeout (1s), and retry limited to connection errors and 5xx, with the budget explained in one comment
UnknownPostcode renders its own 422 JSON through render() and implements ShouldntReport, which is idiomatic exception mapping
The 401 RequestException is reported before the fallback, and transient failures are not reported
Malformed body handled with a concise ternary that throws
Tests are thorough: exact URL and bearer header asserted, quote() return shape checked directly, all failure paths covered, and an exact message asserted for the 404

v.rationale: Both implementations work and behave the same: same retry predicate, same 1.4s per attempt, same 401/404 handling, and the same fallback. Every suite passes. In the probes, both returned 1 call and the fallback for a 429, 2 calls and 1 report for 500 then 401, and a 422 for 500, 500, 404. Both reject Arabic-Indic digits. I found no real bugs in either. My probe that put a string into the fallback config fails in both, but that is contrived because config/services.php casts the value to int. The ranking comes down to idioms. impl-1's tests are clearly more modern: Http::preventStrayRequests, Sleep::fake so retries don't really sleep, Exceptions::fake with assertReported, and named datasets. impl-2's tests do real 100ms sleeps and work around exception reporting by registering reportable() callbacks on the handler. impl-2's code is a bit tidier in places (an exception that renders itself, a shorter connect timeout) but adds a QuoteShipping Action layer and an unneeded ShouldntReport. impl-1 has some ceremony of its own: constants used once and small private helpers. On balance impl-1's better failure-path testing puts it first, narrowly.
